name: List
description: Stacks items down the page with evenly spaced bullets, numbers, or icons.

when: Steps, instructions, or anything with an order
Plain stacks of links in a sidebar
whenNot: Items are pickable (use Menu or Select)
Items need their own surface (use Card in a Grid)
guidelines: Order matters? Use as="ol" so the numbers are real
Keep one icon meaning per list — mixing icons reads as noise
Write items in parallel grammar; scanning depends on it
accessibility: Real ul/ol markup means screen readers announce the item count
Icons are decorative — the text has to carry the meaning

examples.name: Bullet List
examples.description: The default marker — reach for it when order does not matter.

examples.name: Numbered List
examples.description: as="ol" makes the sequence real, not just visual.
examples.code:
<List as="ol" variant="decimal">
  <List.Item>Create your account</List.Item>
  <List.Item>Configure your settings</List.Item>
  <List.Item>Start building</List.Item>
</List>

examples.name: Icon List
examples.description: Each item takes its own icon — checkmarks sell a feature list.
examples.code:
<List variant="icon">
  <List.Item icon={<Check weight="bold" color="var(--fui-color-success)" />}>
    Unlimited projects
  </List.Item>
  <List.Item icon={<Check weight="bold" color="var(--fui-color-success)" />}>
    Priority support
  </List.Item>
  <List.Item icon={<Check weight="bold" color="var(--fui-color-success)" />}>
    Advanced analytics
  </List.Item>
</List>

examples.name: No Style
examples.description: No markers, wider gap — the shape for stacked nav links.

relations.note: Use Icon as List.Item icon prop
Use Stack for non-semantic vertical lists
